matchingCards.excerpt: Binary search and the candidate interval Summary Binary search locates a target in a sorted array by maintaining an interval containing every remaining possible target location. Each unsuccessful midpoint comparison roug…

confirmedCreateAndRetry.absencePassage:
A matching midpoint ends the search successfully. If the interval becomes empty without a match, the target is absent: no possible target location remains.

Each unsuccessful step roughly halves the number of candidates. Repeated halving reduces an array of $n$ elements to at most one candidate after a logarithmic number of steps, so binary search uses $O(\log n)$ comparisons. An initially empty array immediately yields absence.
